The reusable workflow computed the Dockerfile hash, artifact name, artifact
path, output type and push flag across three shell steps, then re-checked in a

ci: fix gate-on-findings to filter by scanner from results.json, not trivy convert

The slim image scan job failed on this branch's PR with "gate failed on
misconfigurations" and "gate failed on detected secrets" - but the printed
table under both errors was the vulnerability table, not misconfig or secret
findings, and that scan never even ran the misconfig scanner (scanners:
vuln,secret).

`trivy convert --scanners X` doesn't filter what counts toward --exit-code;
its own --help says the flag is "used only for rendering the summary table."
So `gate misconfig ...` / `gate secret ...` evaluated the exit code against
the whole report - i.e. against the vulnerabilities that are almost always
present - regardless of whether misconfig or secret findings existed. Verified
against a real Trivy binary: a vuln-only report trips both a misconfig-scanner
and a secret-scanner convert call, printing the same vulnerability table each
time.

This was latent before today: fail_on_secrets was already unconditionally true
on every release/dry-run job, so real release scans have likely been gating on
vulnerabilities under the "secrets" label whenever any vulnerability existed.
Defaulting both to true broadened the blast radius to every build.

Replace the trivy-convert-based gate with direct jq queries against
results.json: vulnerabilities filtered by severity, misconfigurations filtered
to Status=="FAIL", and secrets by presence - each scoped to its own field, so a
gate can never trip on a finding type its scan didn't run.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

ci: run each Trivy scanner separately instead of splitting one report

The gate bug had a second head. `--scanners` is documented as "used only for
rendering the summary table", so besides not filtering --exit-code it does not
filter SARIF either: `trivy convert --scanners vuln --format sarif` and
`--scanners secret` on the same report produce byte-identical files. Every image
scan has therefore been uploading its full vulnerability list twice, once under
the vulnerability category and once under the -Secrets category.

Filtering a mixed report after the fact is the problem. Give each scanner its own
Trivy invocation and its own report file instead, and the table, the SARIF and
the gate are each scoped to one finding type by construction - no filtering flag
anywhere, and no jq. A gate can no longer trip on a finding type its scan never
ran, because it only ever reads its own scanner's file.

The gates go back to being one line each, since a per-scanner report needs no
filtering to interpret: `trivy convert --exit-code 1 secret.json` for secrets and
misconfigurations, plus --severity for vulnerabilities, which does filter
correctly. They also now require their scanner to be in `scanners`, so
fail_on_misconfig defaulting to true no longer reaches an image scan.

Costs one extra Trivy run per additional scanner. Measured on a 51 MB image with
a cold scan cache: 1.1s combined vs 1.9s split, against ~15s of setup and DB
download in the same step, because the second run reuses the cached layer
analysis.
